name: Server triage (Linux)
description: Why did it die, what is eating the disk that you can safely reclaim, and who has been logging in. Linux only.
author: voltius

snippets.name: Why did it die
snippets.description: Recent boots, OOM kills, failed services and the tail of the kernel log.

steps.content:
# The three things that explain "it was working yesterday": a reboot, an OOM
# kill, or a service that gave up.
echo "== Uptime and recent boots =="
uptime
command -v last >/dev/null 2>&1 && last reboot 2>/dev/null | head -5

echo
echo "== OOM kills =="
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RAW=$(journalctl -k --no-pager 2>/dev/null)
  RC=$?
  if [ $RC -ne 0 ] && [ -z "$RAW" ]; then
    echo "kernel log not readable (need root or the adm/systemd-journal group)"
  else
    OUT=$(echo "$RAW" | grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" | tail -20)
    if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "none found — no OOM kill recorded"; fi
  fi
elif [ -r /var/log/kern.log ]; then
  OUT=$(grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" /var/log/kern.log 2>/dev/null | tail -20)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "none found — no OOM kill recorded"; fi
else
  RAW=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null)
  RC=$?
  if [ $RC -ne 0 ] && [ -z "$RAW" ]; then
    echo "dmesg not readable without root"
  else
    OUT=$(echo "$RAW" | grep -iE "out of memory|oom-kill" | tail -20)
    if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then echo "$OUT"; else echo "none found — no OOM kill recorded"; fi
  fi
fi

echo
echo "== Failed services =="
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  systemctl --failed --no-pager
elif command -v rc-status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rc-status --crashed 2>/dev/null || rc-status 2>/dev/null
else
  echo "no service manager found"
fi

echo
echo "== Last 20 kernel messages =="
OUT=$(dmesg 2>/dev/null | tail -20)
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "dmesg not readable without root"
fi

snippets.name: Reclaim disk safely
snippets.description: Shows the size of the journal, package caches and /tmp, then reclaims only those — including deleting journal entries older than 7 days. Never touches images, volumes or your data.

steps.content:
# Only caches and rotated logs are touched. Images, volumes and your data are
# never in scope here — that is what makes this safe to run on a live box.
# The journal vacuum below permanently deletes entries older than 7 days.
echo "== Disk before =="
df -h / | tail -1

echo
echo "== What can be reclaimed =="
[ -d /var/log/journal ] && sudo du -sh /var/log/journal
[ -d /var/cache/apt ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/apt
[ -d /var/cache/dnf ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/dnf
[ -d /var/cache/apk ]   && sudo du -sh /var/cache/apk

echo
# Shown for context only — files here can be in active use, so this script
# never clears /tmp automatically.
echo "== /tmp (shown only — not cleared automatically) =="
sudo du -sh /tmp

echo
echo "== Reclaiming =="
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Deleting journal entries older than 7 days — this permanently removes that history and cannot be undone."
  sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=7d
fi
command -v apt-get    >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo apt-get clean && echo "apt cache cleaned"
command -v dnf        >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo dnf clean all
command -v apk        >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo rm -rf /var/cache/apk/* && echo "apk cache cleaned"

echo
echo "== Disk after =="
df -h / | tail -1

snippets.name: Who logged in
snippets.description: Current sessions, recent logins and failed attempts, from whichever of wtmp, btmp or the journal this host keeps.

steps.content:
# Who has had access recently, and who tried and failed — the first two
# questions after a lockout scare or a suspected intrusion.
echo "== Connected right now =="
OUT=$(who 2>/dev/null || w 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "no active sessions (or no utmp on this host)"
fi

echo
echo "== Last 15 logins =="
OUT=$(last -n 15 2>/dev/null | head -16)
if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
else
  echo "no wtmp on this host"
fi

echo
echo "== Failed attempts =="
if command -v lastb >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(sudo lastb -n 15 | head -16)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no btmp on this host"
  fi
elif command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OUT=$(sudo journalctl -u ssh -u sshd --no-pager | grep -i "failed password" | tail -15)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no failed-password entries found"
  fi
elif [ -r /var/log/auth.log ]; then
  OUT=$(sudo grep -i "failed password" /var/log/auth.log | tail -15)
  if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
    echo "$OUT"
  else
    echo "no failed-password entries found"
  fi
else
  echo "no auth log available"
fi
